item.text:
Refactored the fixture layer so scenarios are now the canonical source of inserted keys, expected traversal, and search expectations. [BTreeScenario.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/046_b_tree/BTreeScenario.java:5) now stores immutable `List<Integer>` data, derives the expected sorted traversal automatically, and builds trees directly from that list. That removed the repeated array-to-list conversions and the duplicated sorted-key expectations that were spread across samples and tests.

I also added iterable-based bulk construction to [BTree.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/046_b_tree/BTree.java:17) with `fromKeys(int, Iterable<Integer>)` and `insertAll(Iterable<Integer>)`, so scenario-backed callers can pass their data without converting back to arrays. With that in place, [BTreeSamples.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/046_b_tree/BTreeSamples.java:2) is just named scenario definitions, and [BTreeTest.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/046_b_tree/BTreeTest.java:23) stays focused on scenario-level behavior instead of hand-maintaining expected traversal data.

Verified with `javac BTree.java BTreeScenario.java BTreeSamples.java BTreeTestSupport.java BTreeTest.java Main.java`, `java -cp . Main`, and `java -cp . BTreeTest`.
